mapper.name: rec
mapper.value:
RECIPE BOOK (built from the 111 stories HealthSignals has published). Identify the story type, then start from its devices; you may invent a better one, but beat these. Every device = one familiar object from the story's world + one twist that shows what changed.
R1 APPROVAL / REGISTRATION (FDA, Anvisa, Cofepris, Digemid, EU nods; e.g. once-weekly insulin, first PROTAC, PrEP twice a year): the product's own packaging receiving the one mark that matters (a blank box getting its first label; a vial with a calendar label showing the new dosing rhythm; a key cut to fit one specific lock = targeted mechanism). Show what is NEW about this approval (dosing, first-in-class, new population), not approval in general.
R2 COVERAGE / FORMULARY / ESSENTIAL LIST (SUS adds drugs, ANS mandates, Caremark adds or drops, Remediar narrows): a pharmacy shelf, formulary binder or pill organiser where items move in or out; for a swap, one box going in while another comes out of the same slot; for a narrowed list, a long shelf reduced to one section. For a gap between coverage and use (coverage without uptake), a full shelf with untouched boxes.
R3 PRICE RULE / REFERENCE PRICE / PRICE CUT (SINPREM caps, Uruguay acquisition price, mandatory generic price cut, Medicare GLOBE benchmark, MFN): a price tag, receipt or till with the twist on the tag itself (a tag with a ceiling line drawn on it; a tag tied to tags from other countries; a receipt being trimmed). Never coins stacks.
R4 BUDGET / FUNDING (Ricarte Soto cut, IHME funding falls, budget lines, mental-health gap): a household-budget object at system scale: an envelope, a piggy bank, a measuring jug, a plate portion; the twist is the size of the share versus the need (a small envelope for a long list; a portion that covers part of the plate).
R5 PROCUREMENT / TENDER / SUPPLY CONTRACTS (Mexico consolidated tender, Sercop idle deals, multi-country imports, BIRMEX contract): an order slip, a delivery crate, a loading dock, a shopping list ticked line by line; for signed-but-idle deals, signed order slips pinned on a board with empty crates below.
R6 PAYER DEBT / UNPAID BILLS / SERVICE SUSPENSION (EPS debts, PAMI fee gap, ADRES credit line): a stack of unpaid invoices, a clinic door sign turned around, a meter running; for a credit line, a bill paid with a ticket that is also a loan note. Never show patients suffering.
R7 COURTS / LITIGATION / ENFORCEMENT (Consejo de Estado orders, 340B suits, compulsory licensing, suspensions, indictments): the rule or the case as a physical object, not a building: a court file with a new tab added (more parties join), a rulebook reopened at a blank chapter (ordered to write a new policy), a patent certificate with a hinge (compulsory licence), a production line paused by a pinned notice (suspension). Neutral: show the procedure, never a side winning.
R8 DEALS / M&A / LICENSING (acquisitions, sublicences, biosimilar partnerships): two objects that fit: a key and a lock, two halves of a pill blister, a plug and a socket, a recipe card handed over (licence), a smaller box fitting a gap in a bigger case; price only if stated.
R9 TRIAL RESULTS (risk cut 58 percent, PSA response, failed outcome despite biomarker drop, device trial head-to-head): the endpoint as an everyday measure: a ruler, a clock, a dial, a road length; positive = the measure visibly moves; mixed (marker falls, outcome does not) = one dial moves while the other stays put. Never bar charts, never patients.
R10 EPIDEMIOLOGY / OUTBREAK / BURDEN (measles surge, PAHO risk, neurological burden, diagnostic wait): a calendar, a map-free tally board, a waiting-room ticket roll, a crowd of identical faceless figures with the stated share in the accent colour (only if the share is in the excerpt); for long diagnostic waits, a ticket roll unwinding across the frame.
R11 MANUFACTURING / INVESTMENT / LOCALISATION (new plant, capacity, local biologics, API exports): the product line itself: a conveyor of vials, a blister press, a pallet; the twist is origin or scale (a production line growing out of a local landscape outline without borders; a shipping label turned from import to export).
R12 MARKET STRUCTURE / PBM / TRANSPARENCY (fee disclosure rules, ownership bans, price-transparency tools): the transaction object made visible: a prescription with its price tag clipped on before the bag is sealed; a receipt printed both sides; an envelope with a window; two parts of a company drawn as a pill splitting along its score line (divestiture).
R13 DIGITAL HEALTH / AI / DATA RULES (CFM AI rules, interoperability pacts, telemedicine standards, online drug sales): the tool with a rule attached: a plug with a new standard socket, a chat window shaped like a prescription pad, a cable joining two different connectors, a shopping cart icon next to a pharmacy counter.
R14 COMPETITION / GENERICS / LAUNCH ORDER (generic race, generic pressure, launch order reshaped by MFN): a starting line or relay, a queue at a counter, identical boxes multiplying beside one branded box; launch order = boxes leaving a dock in a new sequence.
R15 GUIDELINES / SCREENING / CLINICAL PRACTICE (earlier use, newborn screening, reordered treatment): timing and sequence: starting blocks moved, a calendar with an earlier date circled, a sequence of steps where one step moves forward.
R16 ACCESS LAG / REACH (devices arriving years later, a therapy that reaches 30 patients): a long delivery path, a postmark sequence, a door opened only a crack; scale shift between the size of the need and the size of what arrived.
R17 VOICES / INTERVIEWS (quotes from experts): never a portrait; draw the idea of the quote as an object (price to value = a price tag turning into a measuring cup; reckless proposal = a blueprint missing its foundation); the cover line can echo the quote without quotation marks.

mapper.name: bank
mapper.value:
REFERENCE BANK (what HealthSignals' editor has chosen and rejected; learn the pattern, never copy the picture)
WINNERS
+ Optum Rx price tool: a prescription slip marked Rx with a blank price tag clipped to it before it is filled. Why: the story's own object plus one twist; readable without the headline.
+ ADA/EASD earlier GLP-1 and SGLT2: a running track whose starting blocks / starting line has been moved forward. Line: Moving the starting line. Why: guideline timing as a sport everyone knows; neutral; witty.
+ BMS and A.C.Camargo 90-day risk-sharing: a medicine vial whose label is a calendar with one day circled. Line: The 90-day clause. Why: fusion of the product and the contract term; calm.
+ Optum Rx (earlier version): a shopping cart holding one price tag. Line: See before you fill. Why: instant, but less specific than the Rx slip.
+ BMS and A.C.Camargo 90-day risk-sharing (newer): medicine vials dropping into a jar used as a money box. Line: Paid back in kind. Why: the compensation is in vials, not cash; exact and witty.
+ Novartis Lp(a) drug cuts the marker but fails the outcome trial: an auto-injector pen casting a question-mark shadow. Line: Perfect shot. No effect. Why: the paradox in one object.
+ Global health funding falls again: a cracked piggy bank losing a big coin. Line: More out than in.
+ Optum Rx price tool: a restaurant menu listing pills with dotted price lines. Line: The menu before the meal.
LOSERS
- A dipstick painted with EMPLOYER RANGE, BREAK-EVEN and MEDICARE: right idea, ruined by written words.
- Grey figures in suits behind folders at a long table: generic, corporate, no wit.
- A cheque with Pay to the order of and an elderly figure with a cane: text plus patient queue.
- Revolving door labelled 340B: unclear, and a revolving door suggests lobbying (stakeholder risk).
- A weight stamped WEIGHT casting a dollar-sign shadow: clever pun but relies on written words and misses the key fact.
- A pill bottle with a cut-here line and a queue of patients including an elderly figure: reads as a payer cutting patients off (blames a named actor).
- A flame on a gas canister labelled 340B with the line Still lit, for now: hints at a threat and takes a side.
- Blank torn paper with a price tag: the main object is not recognisable.
- Documents full of fake text lines, cards with big words (PRICE WISE): text-heavy, clashes with the headline.
- A ruler with abstract bars; a seesaw with an AETNA block: abstract, reader cannot tell what is being measured.
- Bridges, cliffs, forking roads, umbrellas: the old templates; generic.

mapper.name: cast
mapper.value:
HEALTHSIGNALS CAST (recurring characters for market actors; use them when the story is about who does what to whom). All are simple faceless figures with a round head and no facial features, gender-neutral, same height, same calm posture; each is identified only by one colour and one prop, never by clothes that signal class or occupation, never caricatured.
PATIENT: soft rose figure holding a small paper prescription bag.
PROVIDER (hospital, clinic, physician): sage-green figure holding a clipboard with a chart.
INSURER / HEALTH PLAN / EPS / PAYER: slate-blue figure holding an oversized insurance card.
PBM / INTERMEDIARY: mustard figure holding a long curling receipt.
MANUFACTURER / PHARMA / BIOTECH: burnt-orange figure holding a medicine vial.
REGULATOR (FDA, Anvisa, Cofepris, ANMAT, Digemid): dark-teal figure holding a large rubber stamp.
GOVERNMENT / MINISTRY / PUBLIC SYSTEM: navy figure holding a budget envelope.
COURT: dark-ink figure holding an open rulebook (no robe, wig, gavel or uniform).
EMPLOYER: warm-grey figure holding a payroll envelope.
PHARMACY / RETAILER: terracotta figure behind a small plain counter.
INVESTOR / ACQUIRER: plum figure holding a seedling in a pot.
Rules for the cast: every figure is a plain flat coloured silhouette with no costume, robe, wig, hat, uniform, suit or tie, whatever the rendering style; never fighting, pushing, chasing or towering over each other unless relative size is the stated fact; they may hand things over, queue, sit at a table, stand on a platform, hold opposite ends of an object; no more than four characters in one cover; one character may be the hero, none is the villain.
COUNTRY CUES (when the story is about one country): either paint the main object or the characters' bands in the country's flag colours (never a flag, emblem, coat of arms or map), or add one small iconic, non-political, non-religious place silhouette, only when the country's public system is involved. Brazil: green, yellow, blue; Copacabana wave pavement or Sugarloaf. Mexico: green, white, red; papel picado bunting or the Angel of Independence. Argentina: sky blue and white; the Obelisco. Colombia: yellow, blue, red; coffee hills with wax palms. Chile: red, white, blue; Andes peaks. Peru: red and white; Machu Picchu outline. Panama: red, white, blue; canal locks. Costa Rica: blue, white, red; a volcano cone. Uruguay: blue and white; Palacio Salvo outline. Ecuador: yellow, blue, red; Chimborazo. United States: navy, red, white; the Capitol dome only for federal policy. Never stereotypes: no sombreros, ponchos, carnival costumes, cartels, favelas or tropical fruit clichés.

mapper.name: styles
mapper.value:
STYLE BANK (choose ONE per cover; describe it in the image prompt exactly as written; never name a living artist; never photorealistic people)
S01 PAPERCUT: layered coloured cut paper with soft drop shadows, visible paper fibre.
S02 PAPER SCULPTURE: a small three-dimensional paper model photographed on a table, folded edges, soft studio light, shallow depth of field.
S03 GOUACHE: matte opaque painted colour shapes, visible brush grain, slightly uneven edges.
S04 WATERCOLOUR AND INK: loose transparent washes contained by a confident fine ink line, white paper showing through.
S05 LINOCUT TWO-COLOUR: carved relief print in two inks with slight misregistration and carving marks.
S06 WOODCUT: bold black woodgrain relief print with one spot colour.
S07 RISOGRAPH: two or three soft overlapping inks, visible grain and slight misregistration.
S08 SCREENPRINT POSTER: mid-century flat colour shapes, crisp edges, three to four inks, subtle halftone.
S09 VINTAGE ENGRAVING COLLAGE: nineteenth-century engraved objects cut out and combined with flat colour paper shapes.
S10 MIXED-MEDIA COLLAGE: torn coloured paper, a little printed texture and pencil marks, no photographs of people.
S11 CERAMIC: the main object modelled as a glazed ceramic piece, photographed on a plain surface.
S12 CLAY MINIATURE: a small handmade plasticine scene, fingerprints in the clay, soft light.
S13 WOODEN TOY: painted wooden toy pieces with rounded edges on a plain backdrop.
S14 EMBROIDERY: the image stitched in coloured thread on linen, visible stitches.
S15 PRINTED TIN TOY: lithographed tin object with slightly worn paint.
S16 ISOMETRIC MINIATURE: a tidy isometric diorama, soft shadows, muted colours.
S17 CHARCOAL AND PASTEL: soft charcoal drawing with two pastel colour accents on toned paper.
S18 PENCIL CRAYON: coloured pencil on warm paper, visible hatching in the colour only.
S19 OIL PAINT: thick impasto oil paint, confident strokes, simple composition, still-life feeling.
S20 STAINED GLASS: flat pieces of coloured glass held by dark leading, light glowing through.
S21 MOSAIC: small ceramic tiles forming the image, a calm tile background.
S22 FOLK ART PAINTED TIN: Latin American retablo-like painted metal with bright but harmonious colour, no religious figures.
S23 SILHOUETTE THEATRE: layered cut-card silhouettes on a lit coloured backdrop.
S24 ORIGAMI: the main object folded from a single sheet of coloured paper, crisp creases.
STYLE RULES: if the scene uses cast figures, use only S01, S03, S07, S08, S13 or S23 (flat styles), never engraving, woodcut, oil, charcoal or any style that adds clothing detail; match the style to the story (craft and toy styles for everyday mechanisms; engraving collage and woodcut for law and history; paper sculpture, ceramic and clay for products; folk-art tin, mosaic and embroidery only for Latin American stories); never use the same style family as the previous two covers listed below; colour stays calm and editorial whatever the style.
RECENT STYLES: none yet.
